arxiv-1408-4465.title: Dynamical Stability of Slip-stacking Particles
arxiv-1408-4465.creator: Jeffrey Eldred, Robert Zwaska
arxiv-1408-4465.description: Abstract We study the stability of particles in slip-stacking configuration, used to nearly double proton beam intensity at Fermilab. We introduce universal area factors to calculate the available phase space area for any set of beam parameters without individual simulation. We find perturbative solutions for stable particle trajectories. We establish Booster beam quality requirements to achieve 97% slip-stacking efficiency.

arxiv-2201-12802.title: Berndtsson-Lempert-Szőke Fields associated to Proper Holomorphic Families of Vector Bundles Thanks: Mathematics Subject Classification (2020 Database): 32L05
arxiv-2201-12802.creator: Dror Varolin
arxiv-2201-12802.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dror Varolin. Drawing on work of Berndtsson and of Lempert and Szőke, we define a complex analytic structure for families of (possibly finite-dimensional) Hilbert spaces that might not fit together to form a holomorphic vector bundle but nevertheless have a reasonable definition of curvature that agrees with the curvature of the Chern connection when the family of Hilbert spaces is locally trivial.

arxiv-2202-05922.title: Deep Signatures - Learning Invariants of Planar Curves
arxiv-2202-05922.creator: Roy Velich, Ron Kimmel
arxiv-2202-05922.description: Abstract We propose a learning paradigm for numerical approximation of differential invariants of planar curves. Deep neural-networks’ (DNNs) universal approximation properties are utilized to estimate geometric measures. The proposed framework is shown to be a preferable alternative to axiomatic constructions.

arxiv-2206-14234.title: PyEPO: A PyTorch-based End-to-End Predict-then-Optimize Library for Linear and Integer Programming
arxiv-2206-14234.creator: Bo Tang, Elias B. Khalil
arxiv-2206-14234.description: Abstract In deterministic optimization, it is typically assumed that all problem parameters are fixed and known. In practice, however, some parameters may be a priori unknown but can be estimated from historical data. A typical predict-then-optimize approach separates predictions and optimization into two stages. Recently, end-to-end predict-then-optimize has become an attractive alternative.

arxiv-2210-11643.title: All Politics is Local: Redistricting via Local Fairness Thanks: This work is supported by NSF grants CCF-2113798, IIS-1814493, CCF-2007556, and CCF-2223870.
arxiv-2210-11643.creator: Shao-Heng Ko, Erin Taylor, Pankaj K. Agarwal, Kamesh Munagala
arxiv-2210-11643.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shao-Heng Ko, Erin Taylor, Pankaj K. Agarwal, Kamesh Munagala. In this paper, we propose to use the concept of local fairness for auditing and ranking redistricting plans. Given a redistricting plan, a deviating group is a population-balanced contiguous region in which a majority of individuals are of the same interest and in the minority of their respective districts; such a set of individuals have a justified complaint with how the redistricting plan was drawn.

arxiv-2302-03172.title: High-Dimensional Conditionally Gaussian State Space Models with Missing Data Thanks: A previous version of the paper was circulated under the title “Efficient Estimation of State-Space Mixed-Frequency VARs: A Precision-Based Approach”. We thank Otilia Boldea, Francis Diebold, Gary Koop, James Mitche
arxiv-2302-03172.creator: Joshua C. C. Chan, Aubrey Poon, Dan Zhu
arxiv-2302-03172.description: Abstract We develop an efficient sampling approach for handling complex missing data patterns and a large number of missing observations in conditionally Gaussian state space models. Two important examples are dynamic factor models with unbalanced datasets and large Bayesian VARs with variables in multiple frequencies.

arxiv-2312-13589.title: The anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator in a continuously driven optical lattice
arxiv-2312-13589.creator: Arijit Dutta, Efe Sen, Jun-Hui Zheng, Monika Aidelsburger, Walter Hofstetter
arxiv-2312-13589.description: Abstract The anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator (AFAI) has been theoretically predicted in step-wise periodically driven models, but its stability under more general driving protocols hasn’t been determined. We show that adding disorder to the anomalous Floquet topological insulator realized with a continuous driving protocol in the experiment by K. Wintersperger et. al., Nat. Phys.

arxiv-2404-03638.title: Cooperation between electron-phonon coupling and electronic interaction in bilayer nickelates La 3 Ni 2 O 7
arxiv-2404-03638.creator: Jun Zhan, Yuhao Gu, Xianxin Wu, Jiangping Hu
arxiv-2404-03638.description: Abstract The recent observation of high-T c superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 under pressure has garnered significant interests. While researches have predominantly focused on the role of electron-electron interactions in the superconducting mechanism, the impact of electron-phonon coupling (EPC) has remained elusive.

arxiv-2406-13736.title: Constraining cosmological parameters using void statistics from the SDSS survey
arxiv-2406-13736.creator: Elena Fernández-García, Juan E. Betancort-Rijo, Francisco Prada, Tomoaki Ishiyama, Anatoly Klypin, Julia Ereza

arxiv-2410-08935.creator: Zheng Liu, Haotian Li, Chongjian Yuan, Xiyuan Liu, Jiarong Lin, Rundong Li, Chunran Zheng, Bingyang Zhou, Wenyi Liu, Fu Zhang

In this work, we present Voxel-SLAM: a complete, accurate, and versatile LiDAR-inertial SLAM system that fully utilizes short-term , mid-term , long-term , and multi-map data associations to achieve real-time estimation and high precision mapping.

arxiv-2503-20154.title: The Extreme Faraday Effect in Fast Radio Bursts
arxiv-2503-20154.creator: Yu-Chen Huang, Zi-Gao Dai
arxiv-2503-20154.description: Abstract Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are a type of highly-polarized, millisecond-duration electromagnetic pulses in the radio band, which are mostly produced at cosmological distances. These properties provide a natural laboratory for testing the extreme Faraday effect, a phenomenon in which two different propagation modes of a pulse separate after passing through a dense, highly ionized, and magnetized medium.

pmc-12633790.title: A cadherin-integrin–ECM code for presomitic mesoderm fluidity
pmc-12633790.creator: Miriam A Genuth, Dörthe Jülich, Andrew T Ton, Sarah J Smith, Emilie Guillon, Mark D Shattuck, Corey S O'Hern, Scott A Holley
pmc-12633790.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Animal tissues exist within a continuum of fluid to solid states, and transitions between states are important for embryonic development, wound healing and cancer metastasis. Fluid-to-solid transitions are governed by the ratio of adhesive energy to kinetic energy. Here, we find that presomitic mesoderm solidification is driven by an intrinsic decline in cell speed along with an increase in adhesion mediated by Cadherin 2 in parallel with fibronectin and its receptor Integrin α5.

pmc-13552373.title: Learning from scale-up: a qualitative study of scaling-up interventions for people with multiple long-term conditions in primary care
pmc-13552373.creator: Sarah Chew, Natalie Armstrong, Gregory Maniatopoulos, Neil Perkins, Kamlesh Khunti, Richard Baker, Ash Routen, Janet Willars, Carolyn Tarrant, David Greenfield
pmc-13552373.description: BackgroundScaling innovations for people living with multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs or multimorbidity) remains challenging, particularly in primary care, where organisational capacity, infrastructure, and local contexts vary widely. There is limited empirical understanding of the implementation work needed to navigate these contextual influences when scaling complex innovations across diverse settings.
